questions.stem: A swimmer glides at a constant 2 m/s. How far does she go in 12 s?
questions.explanation: Constant speed: x = vt = 2 × 12 = 24 m.

questions.stem: A car speeds up uniformly from rest to 24 m/s in 6 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: a = Δv/Δt = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 m/s².

questions.stem: A ball is dropped from rest. Ignoring air, what is its speed after 3.0 s? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: v = gt = 9.8 × 3.0 = 29.4 m/s. (44.1 is the distance fallen, in meters.)

questions.stem: Suppose an agent dashes from rest with acceleration 5 m/s² for 2.0 s, then keeps that speed for 3.0 s. What is the total displacement?
questions.explanation: Phase 1: x₁ = ½at² = ½ × 5 × 2² = 10 m, and v = at = 10 m/s. Phase 2: x₂ = vt = 10 × 3 = 30 m. Total = 40 m.

questions.stem: A stone is thrown straight up at 14.7 m/s. How high above the launch point does it rise? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: At the top v = 0, so v² = v₀² − 2gh gives h = v₀²/(2g) = 216.1 ÷ 19.6 ≈ 11.0 m.

questions.stem: In a 50 m pool a swimmer goes down in 20 s, turns, and comes back in 40 s. What is her average speed for the whole 100 m?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 100 ÷ 60 ≈ 1.67 m/s. (The average velocity would be 0, and the mean of the two speeds, 1.88 m/s, is not the answer.)

questions.stem: Car A drives at a constant 20 m/s. Car B starts from rest 100 m behind A at the same moment and accelerates at 2.0 m/s². How long until B catches A?
questions.explanation: Put B at x = 0. B: x = ½(2)t² = t². A: x = 100 + 20t. Set equal: t² − 20t − 100 = 0, so t = 10 + √200 ≈ 24.1 s.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown straight up at 20 m/s from the edge of a 25 m cliff. About how long until it hits the ground at the bottom of the cliff? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Take up as positive and the ground at y = −25: −25 = 20t − 4.9t². So 4.9t² − 20t − 25 = 0 and t = (20 + √(400 + 490)) ÷ 9.8 ≈ 5.1 s. (4.1 s is only the trip back to the cliff edge.)

questions.stem: A 4.0 kg cart accelerates at 3.0 m/s². What is the net force on it?
A 2.0 kg pot sits at rest on a stove. What force does the stove exert on the pot? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: The pot is at rest, so the net force is zero. The stove's normal force balances the weight: N = mg = 2.0 × 9.8 = 19.6 N upward.

questions.stem: A 50 N pull makes a 10 kg box accelerate at 3.0 m/s² along a floor. What is the friction force?
questions.explanation: F_net = ma = 10 × 3 = 30 N. So 50 − f = 30, giving f = 20 N.

questions.stem: A 60 kg swimmer pushes off the wall with an average force of 450 N for 0.40 s. What speed does she gain?
questions.explanation: Impulse = FΔt = 450 × 0.40 = 180 N·s = Δp = mΔv. So Δv = 180 ÷ 60 = 3.0 m/s.

questions.stem: A 5.0 kg block slides down a smooth 30° incline. What is its acceleration? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Along the slope only mg sin θ acts: a = g sin 30° = 9.8 × 0.5 = 4.9 m/s². The mass cancels.

questions.stem: Suppose a 70 kg player stands in an elevator that accelerates upward at 2.0 m/s². What force does the floor push with? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: N − mg = ma, so N = m(g + a) = 70 × 11.8 = 826 N. (686 N is the weight at rest.)

questions.stem: Masses of 3.0 kg and 5.0 kg hang from a light rope over a frictionless pulley. What is the tension in the rope? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: System: a = (5 − 3)g ÷ (5 + 3) = 2.45 m/s². For the 3.0 kg mass going up: T − mg = ma, so T = 3.0 × (9.8 + 2.45) = 36.75 ≈ 37 N. (39 N is the wrong 'average weight' idea.)

questions.stem: A box slides down a 30° incline with kinetic friction coefficient 0.20. What is its acceleration? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Along the slope: a = g(sin θ − μ cos θ) = 9.8 × (0.500 − 0.20 × 0.866) = 9.8 × 0.327 ≈ 3.2 m/s². (Note N = mg cos θ, not mg.)

questions.stem: What is the kinetic energy of a 2.0 kg object moving at 3.0 m/s?
A 55 kg diver climbs onto a 3.0 m platform. By how much does her gravitational potential energy increase? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
A 1.0 kg cart moving at 4.0 m/s hits a 3.0 kg cart at rest and they stick together. What is their speed afterwards?
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 1.0 × 4.0 = (1.0 + 3.0) × v, so v = 1.0 m/s.

questions.stem: A ball is dropped from rest at a height of 5.0 m. Ignoring air, how fast is it moving just before it hits the floor? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Suppose an 80 kg agent running at 5.0 m/s grabs a stationary 60 kg teammate and they move off together. What is their speed?
A 1500 W kettle runs for 3.0 minutes. How much energy does it use?
questions.explanation: E = Pt = 1500 W × 180 s = 270 000 J = 270 kJ. (Convert minutes to seconds first.)

questions.stem: A 2.0 kg block slides at 6.0 m/s on a frictionless floor into a spring with k = 200 N/m. What is the maximum compression of the spring?
questions.explanation: All KE becomes spring energy: ½mv² = ½kx². So x = v√(m/k) = 6.0 × √(2.0 ÷ 200) = 6.0 × 0.10 = 0.60 m.

questions.stem: A 10 g bullet moving at 400 m/s embeds in a 1.99 kg block hanging from strings (the block and bullet together are 2.00 kg). How high do they swing? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Step 1, momentum: 0.010 × 400 = 2.00 × v, so v = 2.0 m/s. Step 2, energy: h = v²/(2g) = 4.0 ÷ 19.6 ≈ 0.20 m.

questions.stem: An object moves around a circle of radius 2.0 m at a constant 4.0 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
A fan blade turns at 5.0 revolutions per second. What is its period?
Wet salad leaves at the edge of a spinner basket of radius 0.10 m move at 2.0 m/s. What is their centripetal acceleration?
A 20 N force pulls on a wrench handle 0.30 m from the bolt, at 30° to the handle. What is the torque on the bolt?
A 1000 kg car takes a flat circular curve of radius 20 m. The coefficient of static friction is 0.50. What is the greatest speed without slipping? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Friction supplies the centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r, so v = √(μgr) = √(0.50 × 9.8 × 20) = √98 ≈ 9.9 m/s.

questions.stem: A solid circular pizza stone (a disk, I = ½MR²) has mass 2.0 kg and radius 0.25 m. A net torque of 0.25 N·m acts on it. What is its angular acceleration?
questions.explanation: I = ½ × 2.0 × 0.25² = 0.0625 kg·m². α = τ/I = 0.25 ÷ 0.0625 = 4.0 rad/s². (2.0 comes from using the ring formula I = MR².)

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg ball on a 1.0 m string is whirled in a vertical circle. At the very top its speed is 5.0 m/s. What is the tension in the string there? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: At the top both tension and weight point down, toward the center: T + mg = mv²/r. T = 0.50 × 25 ÷ 1.0 − 0.50 × 9.8 = 12.5 − 4.9 = 7.6 N.

questions.stem: A diver in layout position (I = 3.0 kg·m², ω = 2.0 rad/s) tucks so that I = 1.2 kg·m². By what factor does her rotational kinetic energy change?
questions.explanation: Angular momentum is conserved: ω₂ = 3.0 × 2.0 ÷ 1.2 = 5.0 rad/s. KE = ½Iω²: before 6.0 J, after ½ × 1.2 × 25 = 15 J. Ratio 15 ÷ 6.0 = 2.5. (The extra energy comes from her muscles.)

questions.stem: A kitchen spring with k = 50 N/m is stretched 0.20 m by a pan. What is the spring force?
An oscillator completes 30 cycles in 12 s. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: f = cycles ÷ time = 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5 Hz.

questions.stem: A lifeguard's whistle hangs on a 1.0 m string and swings as a simple pendulum. What is its period? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
A 0.50 kg mass hangs from a spring with k = 200 N/m. What is the period of its vertical oscillation?
A spring scale in a kitchen bounces with a load. If the load mass is quadrupled, the period changes by what factor?
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k) so T ∝ √m. Quadruple m gives √4 = 2 times the period.

questions.stem: An oscillator has amplitude 0.10 m and angular frequency 4.0 rad/s. What is its maximum speed?
questions.explanation: v_max = Aω = 0.10 × 4.0 = 0.40 m/s, reached at x = 0.

questions.stem: A 0.40 kg mass on a spring (k = 100 N/m) oscillates with amplitude 0.10 m. What is its speed when x = 0.060 m?
A pendulum has period 2.0 s on the ground. It is carried in an elevator that accelerates upward at 2.45 m/s² (= g/4). What is its period now?
questions.explanation: Upward acceleration makes the effective gravity g_eff = g + g/4 = 1.25g. T ∝ 1/√g_eff, so T = 2.0 ÷ √1.25 = 2.0 ÷ 1.118 ≈ 1.8 s.

questions.stem: The distance between two planets doubles. The gravitational force between them becomes…
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r². Doubling r divides F by 2² = 4.

questions.stem: A 2.0 kg bag of rice sits on a kitchen scale. What is the gravitational force on it? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
A 70 kg swimmer visits the Moon, where g = 1.6 m/s². What is her weight there?
questions.explanation: W = mg = 70 × 1.6 = 112 N. Her mass is still 70 kg. (686 N is her weight on Earth.)

questions.stem: At what distance from Earth's center is g one quarter of its surface value, if the surface is at distance R?
questions.explanation: g ∝ 1/r². For g/4 we need r² four times larger, so r = 2R (that is, R above the surface).

questions.stem: Suppose a new map is set on a planet with 4 times Earth's mass and 2 times Earth's radius. What is its surface gravity? (Earth: 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: g = GM/R². Mass ×4 and radius² ×4 cancel, so g is unchanged: 9.8 m/s².

questions.stem: A satellite orbits at r = 6.77 × 10⁶ m from Earth's center. Using G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² and M = 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, what is its orbital speed?
Two satellites circle the same planet. Satellite B's orbital radius is 4 times that of satellite A. B's period is how many times A's?
questions.explanation: Kepler's third law: T² ∝ r³. So T ∝ r^(3/2) = 4^(3/2) = 8.

questions.stem: The Moon's mass is 1/81 of Earth's. On the line between them, where do their gravitational pulls on a small probe cancel? Give the distance from Earth as a fraction of the Earth–Moon distance D.
questions.explanation: Set M/x² = (M/81)/(D − x)². Taking square roots: (D − x)/x = 1/9, so 9D − 9x = x and x = 0.90 D.

questions.stem: A 6.0 Ω resistor is connected across a 12 V battery. What is the current?
A toaster is rated 1200 W on a 120 V supply. What current does it draw?
Two identical 4.0 Ω heating elements in a pool heater are wired in series. What is their combined resistance?
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: 4.0 + 4.0 = 8.0 Ω.

questions.stem: An 8.0 Ω and a 24 Ω resistor are in parallel across a 24 V battery. What total current does the battery supply?
A 2000 W kettle runs for 3.0 minutes. How much electrical energy is that in kilowatt-hours?
A 10 μF capacitor is charged to 12 V. How much energy does it store?
A 12 V battery drives current through a 4.0 Ω resistor in series with a parallel pair of 6.0 Ω and 12 Ω resistors. What power is dissipated in the 12 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: Parallel pair: (6 × 12) ÷ 18 = 4.0 Ω. Total = 8.0 Ω, I = 1.5 A. Voltage across the pair = 1.5 × 4.0 = 6.0 V. P = V²/R = 36 ÷ 12 = 3.0 W.

questions.stem: Capacitors of 6.0 μF and 3.0 μF are connected in series to a 9.0 V battery. What charge is on the 3.0 μF capacitor?
questions.explanation: In series, 1/C = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so C = 2.0 μF. Q = CV = 2.0 × 9.0 = 18 μC, and series capacitors all carry the same charge.

questions.stem: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. What is its change in internal energy?
questions.explanation: First law: ΔU = Q − W = 500 − 200 = +300 J.

questions.stem: Heat always flows from a hot pan into cold water, never the other way by itself. Which law says this?
questions.explanation: The direction of spontaneous heat flow, and the rising entropy, is the second law of thermodynamics.

questions.stem: A pool is at 25 °C. What is that temperature in kelvin?
A Carnot engine runs between 500 K and 300 K. What is its maximum efficiency?
A heat engine takes 800 J from a hot reservoir and does 200 J of work. How much heat does it reject to the cold reservoir?
questions.explanation: Energy balance: Q_c = Q_h − W = 800 − 200 = 600 J.

questions.stem: A cook stirs soup, doing 150 J of work on it, while 40 J of heat leaves the pot. What is the change in the soup's internal energy?
questions.explanation: Work done ON the system is W = −150 J (by the system). ΔU = Q − W = −40 − (−150) = +110 J.

questions.stem: An inventor claims an engine working between 400 K and 300 K takes in 1000 J of heat and does 300 J of work. Is that possible?

choices.A: Possible: it equals the Carnot limit of 30%
choices.B: Possible: 30% is below the Carnot limit of 75%
choices.C: Possible if all friction is removed
choices.D: Impossible: it rejects 700 J, more than the 300 J of work
choices.E: Impossible: 30% is above the Carnot limit of 25%

questions.explanation: Carnot limit: e = 1 − 300/400 = 25%. The claimed efficiency is 300/1000 = 30%, larger than the best possible, so the claim breaks the second law.

questions.stem: A Carnot engine has efficiency 40% with a cold reservoir at 300 K. To raise its efficiency to 60% with the same cold reservoir, to what temperature must the hot reservoir be raised?
How much heat is needed to warm 0.50 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C? (c = 4186 J/(kg·K))
The Sun warms Earth across empty space. Which heat transfer method is this?
questions.explanation: There is no material between the Sun and Earth, so only radiation (electromagnetic waves) can carry the heat.

questions.stem: A pool holds 1000 kg of water. How much heat raises its temperature by 1.0 K? (c = 4186 J/(kg·K))
questions.explanation: Q = mcΔT = 1000 × 4186 × 1.0 = 4.19 × 10⁶ J ≈ 4.2 MJ. Water's big c is why pools warm slowly.

questions.stem: How much heat melts 0.30 kg of ice at 0 °C? (L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J/kg)
A cook pours 200 g of 80 °C water into 300 g of 20 °C water. Ignoring losses, what is the final temperature?
Equal masses of A and B get the same heat. A warms by 20 K and B warms by 10 K. What is c_A divided by c_B?
questions.explanation: Q = mcΔT with equal Q and m means c ∝ 1/ΔT. So c_A/c_B = 10/20 = 0.50.

questions.stem: How much heat turns 0.10 kg of ice at −10 °C into liquid water at 100 °C? (c_ice = 2100, c_water = 4186 J/(kg·K); L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J/kg)
A 0.50 kg metal block at 200 °C is dropped into 2.0 kg of pool water at 20 °C. The final temperature is 22 °C. What is the metal's specific heat? (c_water = 4186 J/(kg·K))
questions.explanation: Heat gained by water = 2.0 × 4186 × 2 = 16 744 J. Heat lost by metal = 0.50 × c × (200 − 22) = 89c. So c = 16 744 ÷ 89 ≈ 188 J/(kg·K).

questions.stem: A gas in a rigid container is heated from 300 K to 600 K. By what factor does its pressure change?
questions.explanation: At constant V, P ∝ T (kelvin). Doubling T doubles P.

questions.stem: A sealed pressure cooker holds air at 100 kPa and 300 K. It is heated to 450 K. What is the pressure now (volume fixed)?
A pool pump traps 2.0 L of air at 100 kPa and squeezes it at constant temperature to 0.50 L. What is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: Boyle: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so P₂ = 100 × 2.0 ÷ 0.50 = 400 kPa.

questions.stem: How many moles of gas are in 2.0 L at 300 K and 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa? (R = 8.315 J/(mol·K))
A diver's air bubble has volume 2.0 mL at 20 m depth, where the pressure is 3.0 atm. What is its volume at the surface (1.0 atm), at the same temperature?
questions.explanation: Boyle: V₂ = V₁P₁/P₂ = 2.0 × 3.0 ÷ 1.0 = 6.0 mL.

questions.stem: A gas expands at a constant pressure of 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa from 1.0 L to 4.0 L. How much work does the gas do?
A fixed amount of gas starts at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K. It is heated and compressed until its pressure is 3 times larger and its volume is half as big. What is the new temperature?
questions.explanation: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂, so T₂ = T₁ × (P₂/P₁)(V₂/V₁) = 300 × 3 × 0.5 = 450 K.

questions.stem: A monatomic ideal gas expands at constant pressure and does 400 J of work. How much heat was added? (For this gas Q = (5/2)PΔV at constant pressure.)
questions.explanation: Work W = PΔV = 400 J. Q = (5/2)PΔV = 2.5 × 400 = 1000 J. The first law checks: ΔU = Q − W = 600 J = (3/2)PΔV.

questions.stem: A 440 Hz tone travels at 343 m/s in air. What is its wavelength?
Which property of a sound wave sets its pitch?
questions.explanation: Higher frequency means higher pitch. Amplitude sets loudness.

questions.stem: Suppose a footstep cue in a game echoes back from a far wall after 0.40 s. If sound moves at 343 m/s, how far away is the wall?
questions.explanation: The sound goes there and back, so d = vt/2 = 343 × 0.40 ÷ 2 = 68.6 ≈ 69 m.

questions.stem: Sound travels at about 1480 m/s in water. How long does a splash sound take to cross 37 m of pool water?
questions.explanation: t = d/v = 37 ÷ 1480 = 0.025 s. (In air it would take 0.11 s.)

questions.stem: A blender is 90 dB and a quiet kitchen is 60 dB. How many times greater is the blender's sound intensity?
questions.explanation: Every 10 dB is a factor of 10 in intensity. 30 dB more is 10³ = 1000 times.

questions.stem: The speed of sound in air is about v = 331 + 0.6T m/s, where T is in °C. What is it at 30 °C?
A pipe closed at one end is 0.25 m long. What is its fundamental frequency? (v = 343 m/s)
questions.explanation: A closed pipe has a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, so L = λ/4. λ = 1.00 m and f = v/λ = 343 Hz. (686 Hz would be an open pipe.)

questions.stem: You stand between two cliffs and clap. You hear echoes 0.50 s and 1.20 s later. If sound moves at 343 m/s, how far apart are the cliffs?
questions.explanation: Distances: d₁ = 343 × 0.50 ÷ 2 = 85.8 m and d₂ = 343 × 1.20 ÷ 2 = 205.8 m. You are between them, so the gap is 85.8 + 205.8 ≈ 292 m.
